review_candidates.title: Remote Regional Healthcare Senior Finance Manager - Surgical Practices - TBS and TSS
review_candidates.description: Overview The US Oncology Network is looking for a Remote Regional Healthcare Senior Finance Manager - Texas Breast Specialist and Texas Surgical Specialists to join our team. This role offers the opportunity to influence enterprise strategy, partner closely with senior leadership, and drive meaningful business impact in a complex healthcare envorionment. Must currently reside in Texas. Preferred locations include Austin, Dallas, Houston, and San Antonio. Sites Include: Texas Breast Specialist and Texas Surgical Specialists Statewide Travel: This position is fully remote with up to 25% travel for key meetings. As a part of The US Oncology Network , Texas Oncology delivers high-quality, evidence-based care to patients close to home. Texas Oncology is the largest community oncology provider in the country and has approximately 600+ providers in 300+ sites across Texas, our founders pioneered community-based cancer care because they believed in making the best available cancer care accessible to all communities, allowing people to fight cancer at home with the critical support of family and friends nearby. Our mission is still the same today—at Texas Oncology, we use leading-edge technology and research to deliver high-quality, evidence-based cancer care to help our patients achieve “More breakthroughs. More victories.” ® in their fight against cancer. Today, Texas Oncology treats half of all Texans diagnosed with cancer on an annual basis. The US Oncology Network is one of the nation’s largest networks of community-based oncology physicians dedicated to advancing cancer care in America. The US Oncology Network is supported by McKesson Corporation focused on empowering a vibrant and sustainable community patient care delivery system to advance the science, technology, and quality of care. Why work for us? Come join our team that is responsible for helping lead Texas Oncology in treating more patient diagnosed with cancer than any other provider in Texas. Our Information Technology team offers an outstanding family-first team culture. Extremely low turn-over with long-tenured team members. There are opportunities for career development, excellent benefits and perks as well as self-directed daily work. We offer our employees a competitive benefits package that includes Medical, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance, Short-term and Long-term disability coverage, a generous PTO program, a 401k plan that comes with a company match, a Wellness program that rewards you practicing a healthy lifestyle, and lots of other great perks such as Tuition Reimbursement, an Employee Assistance program and discounts on some of your favorite retailers. Join a Team That Invests in Your Future At Texas Oncology, we recognize the long-term impact of our people and are committed to rewarding performance and potential. That’s why select roles may be eligible to participate in our Long-Term Incentive Plan (LTIP): an incentive program designed to attract, retain, and reward top talent. What is the Long-Term Incentive Plan (LTIP)? Long-Term Incentive Plan (LTIP): is an incentive program that typically vests over a three-year period and is tied to both individual performance and the operational success of Texas Oncology. Awards are discretionary and based on your position, performance, and potential for future career growth at Texas Oncology. Awards are reviewed and approved during the annual compensation review. LTIP awards are subject to your continued employment through the award payment date, and are governed by the written terms and conditions of the LTIP document. What does the Regional Senior Finance Manager do? The Regional Senior Finance Manager is a key finance partner supporting the Division Finance Director and practice leadership across a Texas Oncology region. This role combines hands‑on operational finance with strong analytical capabilities, delivering accurate reporting, actionable insights, and disciplined execution to improve financial performance at the practice level. The Senior Finance Manager collaborates closely with Operations, Controllers, and physician/practice leaders to support budgeting and forecasting, provide meaningful variance analysis, and ensure consistent application of financial processes and controls. This role plays a critical part in advancing growth, efficiency, and performance goals aligned with the long‑range plan. This is an individual contributor role with no direct reports. Supports and adheres to the US Oncology Compliance Program, to include the Code of Ethics and Business Standards. Responsibilities The essential duties and responsibilities (including but not limited to): Financial Planning & Analysis Prepare monthly financial reporting packages, variance analyses, and KPI dashboards for practice and regional leadership. Support annual budgeting and recurring forecast cycles; coordinate inputs, validate assumptions, and maintain driver‑based financial models. Translate financial results into clear insights and recommendations; proactively identify and escalate risks and opportunities to the Division Finance Director. Physician & Practice Engagement Partner with physician and practice leaders to review financial results, productivity trends, and cost drivers. Prepare and present financial materials for practice operations, physician meetings, and board discussions. Serve as the finance liaison and voice for the region, providing responsive, accurate, and customer‑focused support for ad hoc requests. Performance Metrics & Decision Support Maintain and enhance key performance indicators (KPIs), including volume, revenue yield, payor mix/discounts, expense run rates, and working capital metrics. Support the development and enhancement of decision‑support tools in partnership with the Division Finance Director. Capital Planning & Expenditures Support capital expenditure (CapEx) intake and evaluation, including gathering business cases, preparing financial analyses (ROI/NPV), and tracking approved projects against budget and timelines. Promote adherence to internal controls, financial policies, and governance standards. review_candidates.title: Program Manager
review_candidates.description: What This Role Is Every year, hundreds of thousands of students across India decide they want to study abroad. Some come through K12 school partnerships, some find their way in directly. Either way, they enter a journey - discovery, counseling, application, offer, enrollment - that runs through dozens of handoffs between people, platforms, and teams. When that journey works, a student ends up at a university that fits their budget, their course, and their ambitions, and the business realizes revenue at the moment they enroll. When it doesn't, applications stall, deadlines slip, and a student who could have enrolled goes quiet. The problem is not that any single team is failing. It's that the highest-leverage work in a business like this doesn't live inside one function - it lives in the transformation and optimization projects that cut across Tech, Product, Marketing, and Operations, and someone needs to own them end to end. A funnel improvement that Marketing wants tested needs Product to build it and Tech to ship it. A new process that could remove a structural inefficiency needs someone to design it, prove it, and hand it off cleanly. Right now, that ownership happens informally, project by project, and the work that would compound doesn't get the sustained, disciplined execution it needs. This is where this role sits. You will run multiple 'Strategize - Build - Operate - Transfer' projects a year - some of them genuinely 0-1 (new ideas that need user research, market research, and hypothesis testing before anyone knows if they work), some of them optimization projects on things that already exist but need better process design and a new benchmark for what good looks like. You will also be asked to take on whatever else is critical for the business to win, even when it doesn't have a job title yet. You will own full-cycle delivery for these projects - from framing the problem with the right stakeholders, through build and testing, to launch, operating it long enough to prove it works, and transferring it cleanly to whoever owns it long-term. You are the person who makes sure a project doesn't just get discussed. It gets shipped, it gets proven, and it gets handed off in a state someone else can run with. What Makes This Role Different Most program management roles ask you to track a roadmap someone else designed. This one asks you to build the roadmap itself - deciding what the next transformation or optimization project should even be, then owning it across three or four functions that don't naturally report to the same person. The Strategize-Build-Operate-Transfer model means you don't hand a project off the moment it launches; you stay accountable until it's actually working and someone else can run it without you. The Manifest ecosystem gives this role real range: some projects will be genuinely 0-1 - a new idea nobody has tested yet - and others will be 1-100 - scaling something that already works but is starting to strain under its own complexity. Few program roles at this stage give you exposure to both ends of that spectrum in the same year. This is a build role, not a maintenance one. There is no finished playbook for how these projects should run - you're expected to design the frameworks, set the benchmarks, and prove through disciplined experimentation what should scale and what shouldn't. What You Own Transformation projects (Strategize - Build - Operate - Transfer) Translate a business problem into a project plan that Tech, Product, Marketing and Business teams can actually execute against Own the full lifecycle of assigned projects - scoping, stakeholder alignment, build, testing, launch, and post-launch review Own multiple SBOT-cycle projects a year, end to end, from initial strategy through a clean operational handoff Define what "operate" looks like well enough to prove a project works before transferring ownership Ensure nothing gets handed off half-finished - the transfer is only complete when the receiving team can run it without you 0-1 initiatives Lead user research, market research, and hypothesis testing on new ideas before committing resources to build them Design and run experiments that give a clear read on whether an idea is worth scaling Turn ambiguous, early-stage problems into a testable plan within weeks, not quarters Optimization and process design Identify structural inefficiencies across the business and turn them into scoped optimization projects Build the frameworks and process designs that make a function run better, not just faster Set new benchmarks for what "good" looks like once a process has been redesigned Cross-functional execution and influence Be the connective layer between Tech, Product, Marketing, and Operations so a project doesn't stall in the gap between roadmaps Lead cross-functional execution through credibility, influence, and clear decision-making rather than formal authority Take on whatever else is critical for the business to win, even without a predefined mandate What Success Looks Like The markers below reflect where Student Placements is today. We'll calibrate the specifics once you're in the seat. These are directional, not fixed. In your first weeks, you're not shipping yet - you're building a working map of how projects actually move through Tech, Product, and Marketing today, and forming a point of view on where the highest-leverage transformation or optimization opportunities sit. You'll know you're on track when stakeholders start coming to you before a project stalls, not after. By the middle of your first year, you've run at least one full SBOT cycle from strategy to clean handoff, and the people around you trust that if you've said something will happen, it will. You've proven, through real experiments rather than opinion, which 0-1 ideas are worth scaling and which aren't. Longer term, the way the business runs cross-functional projects looks different because you built it that way - frameworks that outlast the specific projects they were built for, a track record of transformations that actually stuck, and a reputation as the person who gets called in when something critical and undefined needs to happen. The specifics will be calibrated once you're in the role. The direction won't change. What You Bring You've spent five to eight years building things inside high-growth environments, and you've likely seen both ends of that growth curve - the 0-1 phase, where the job is rapid experimentation, hypothesis testing, and getting an MVP in front of real users, and the 1-100 phase, where the job becomes process design and managing the complexity that scale creates. You know which mode a problem calls for and you don't try to apply 1-100 rigor to a 0-1 problem, or vice versa. You have real comfort operating in ambiguity, and more than that, you're fast at moving from ambiguity to clarity - you ask the right question early, you don't wait for someone to hand you a clean brief, and you get to a workable answer quickly rather than a perfect one slowly. You think in first principles. When a process is broken, you don't default to the existing framework - you rebuild the logic from the ground up and design something better, then prove it works before asking anyone to trust it. Most importantly, you read the description of what this role is building and your first reaction was not "this sounds like a coordination job." It was "this is exactly the kind of ambiguous, high-leverage problem I want to be handed." That's the person this role is for. Why Manifest Manifest Global is building the infrastructure for global human capital mobility - connecting students, schools, universities, and employers across 50+ countries. Our portfolio spans Cialfo (AI-powered college counseling, 2,000+ schools), BridgeU (university guidance for international schools globally), Kaaiser (trusted study abroad counseling since 1997 across India and Southeast Asia), and Explore (AI-powered university outreach, 1,000+ university partners). Together, we move talent across borders at scale. $700B flows annually in remittances from migrant workers. 85M workers will be missing from developed economies by 2030. We're building the operating system which changes that. $80M raised. Still early. Student Placements is where that infrastructure meets an individual student's decision - and the transformation and optimization work this role owns is what makes that infrastructure work better at every scale it operates at. Manifest Global is building the infrastructure for global human capital mobility, operating across 50+ countries.

Manage annual budgets, monitor financial performance, and implement corrective actions as needed. Establish and track operational KPIs related to cost, quality, delivery, productivity, utilization, and customer satisfaction. Identify operational risks, project deviations, resource constraints, and cost issues, implementing corrective measures. Drive continuous improvement initiatives to enhance efficiency, profitability, quality, and overall operational performance. Optimize working capital and resource utilization across operations. Ensure projects and services meet customer expectations for quality, schedule, responsiveness, and technical standards. Maintain strong relationships with shipowners, vessel operators, shipyards, engineering teams, suppliers, contractors, and stakeholders. Comprehensive understanding of project execution, budgeting, cost control, resource planning, and operational performance. Familiarity with continuous improvement and operational KPI development, working directly with clients such as shipowners, operators, shipyards, and marine contractors. This position is ideal for a seasoned marine operations leader who understands both the technical and business aspects of marine systems.
